Meeting header:
Date: 2025-06-09
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendes (CTO - Nimbus), Amira Haddad (Head of ML - Nimbus), Liam O'Connor (SRE - Nimbus)

Summary (auto): weekly check-in for POC, move from tuning to rollout planning, canary strategy and monitoring, action items captured.

[00:00] Jordan: yeah hey everyone thanks for joining the POC weekly, I see the usual crew, we'll focus on the rollout / go-live checklist today and make sure we have a safe canary plan.
[00:12] Carlos: sounds good, we're excited to move some traffic, we've finished the prompt tuning and the latency looks stable in stage but we want a clear cutover plan.
[00:20] Priya: great, quick note, during the perf runs we saw 95th latency around 380ms on average with the quantized variant, tail spikes up to ~520ms on synthetic bursts, that's when KV cache wasn't warm.
[00:35] Amira: right, and accuracy regressions were minimal after tuning but we still want monitoring on top-K rerank scores for the first week.
[00:44] Liam: from SRE side, we need the VPC peering in place and the audit log stream to our SIEM, plus a small runbook for page triggers.
[00:53] Jordan: ok so proposed canary: start at 5% traffic for 2 hours, monitor error rate, latencies and model quality metrics, then escalate to 20% for 6 hours if healthy, then 50% next day and full at 100% after 48 hours stable. Sounds reasonable?
[01:08] Carlos: 5% -> 20% -> 50% sounds good, can we add a faster rollback path if we see high error rate? like immediate cut to fallback model and route to hosted retried endpoints?
[01:18] Priya: yes, recommend immediate rollback triggers: error rate > 0.5% sustained for 5 minutes OR 95th latency > 700ms for 10 minutes. If triggered we automatically switch routing policy to fallback model (smaller model variant) and then stop the canary. We'll include the exact curl/CLI steps in the runbook.
[01:33] Amira: and can we also have automatic KV cache warm-up before canary to avoid cold-triggered spikes?
[01:40] Priya: absolutely - we can run a prefix-warm job that replays a warmup set; that'll be part of the checklist. We also recommend running a synthetic load for 30 minutes pre-cutover.
[01:52] Liam: on logs, we need the request/response sampling and tracing to come through to Datadog - can Redwood push a sample integration?
[01:59] Jordan: yes, Priya will share the Datadog dashboard JSON and the Redwood Console dashboard link. We'll also include tracing hooks and an example span payload.
[02:10] Carlos: fine, we also have compliance questions — SOC 2 and KMS key access for production keys. We're on SOC 2 Type II and we need to confirm Redwood's audit logs retention.
[02:20] Priya: Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and we can provide audit log configuration. For hosted POC we can forward audit logs to your SIEM via syslog; I'll include the security doc link in the follow-up.
[02:32] Amira: perfect. Also about canary timing — we prefer a business-hours cutover for the first canary so we can respond quickly. Carlos, can you confirm your business hours?
[02:41] Carlos: yes, 9am-6pm EDT, we prefer mid-week. How about Tuesday next week (2025-06-17) morning window?
[02:49] Jordan: works for Redwood, we should then schedule a 2-hour window starting 13:00 UTC to align. We'll put on the calendar tentatively.
[02:58] Priya: checklist items to include in runbook: pre-warm KV cache, synthetic load test, create canary routing rule (5% traffic), Datadog + Redwood Console monitors, rollback CLI commands, communications play (who to page), cost-guardrails (burst cap and expected tokens).
[03:14] Liam: for the routing policy, we need the exact model version pinned and a fallback variant. Also want to confirm we can throttle cost if token spend exceeds threshold.
[03:23] Priya: yes, routing supports version pinning and auto-fallback. For cost-guardrails we recommend dedicated burst capacity with a hard cap and an alert if spend rate exceeds projected by 20%. Jordan will send pricing addendum.
[03:35] Carlos: ok that's good. We also want to test end-to-end from our checkout flow to make sure user visible latencies are acceptable.
[03:43] Amira: and we'll capture quality regressions with our eval set, we'll wire the eval webhook to Redwood Optimize so we get regression alerts.
[03:51] Jordan: action owners recapped: Priya drafts runbook and dashboards; Liam validates VPC and SIEM ingestion; Carlos confirms cutover window and the on-call list; Jordan sends pricing and runbook link.
[04:05] Carlos: one more ask — can Redwood provide a short A/B test template (50/50) for measuring CTR differences over 1 week? we might want a slower experiment after canary.
[04:14] Priya: yes we have an A/B playbook, we'll attach the template and expected metrics to monitor (CTR, mean engagement time, latency delta).
[04:24] Amira: what's the expected warm-up time for cache to reach stable hit-rate?
[04:29] Priya: usually 30-60 minutes of replay depending on prefix overlap; we'll include a recommended warm-up set and script.
[04:36] Liam: regarding security again, we need SAML SSO config for production console access and RBAC mapping to our groups.
[04:44] Jordan: Redwood supports SAML and granular RBAC for workspaces. Priya will include steps for SSO and role mapping.
[04:52] Carlos: great, anything else?
[04:55] Jordan: quick note on SLA expectations — during the canary we won't change hardware, but after full rollout we can propose Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput. Jordan: we'll follow up with committed options and expected latency SLAs.
[05:08] Amira: thanks, appreciate the clarity.
[05:10] Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll send the runbook, dashboard links, pricing and calendar invite for the canary window.
[05:16] End meeting.
